newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close weaker and at lows, specs sell.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close weaker and at lows, specs sell.

text.p: FCOJ futures attempted to consolidate recent losses but failed to hold gains amid steady speculative selling and closed at session lows, traders said.
"The trade was a decent buyer but the specs absorbed a lot of buying," a broker said.
Speculators are expected to continue to chip away at prices amid a negative technical outlook and a bearish supply and demand situation.

Nearby support seen at the recent low of 74.90 cents a lb, followed by 74.30 and then 72.00 cents, for July cotton. The contract ended 0.60 cent lower at 76.60 cents after trading from 77.65 to a two-week low of 77.00 cents. July cotton fetched 74.90 cents on May 12.
Second-position September settled down 0.55 at 79.10 cents, while the rest finished down 0.70 to up 1.80 cents.
"The downtrend is likely to persist with no shortage of juice anticipated this season or next," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said in a weekly citrus comment.
USDA will release its next estimate of the Florida crop on June 12. The crop was forecast at a record 224.2 million 90-lb boxes, and yields at 1.58 gallons per box.
An estimated 3,100 lots changed hands on the day, compared to Thursday's official 2,987 lots.
